newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China says no plans to send oil delegation to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: China says no plans to send oil delegation to Iraq.

text.p: China does not have any immediate plan to send an oil delegation to Iraq to consider upstream oil developments, but officials from the two countries are maintaining contact, a Chinese official said on Tuesday.

"We know several countries, including France and Russia, are interested in Iraq's oilfields. We are speeding up our studies and we've been keeping contact," an official of Chinese National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) said from Beijing.
But CNPC would not go ahead with any concrete plans unless United Nations trade curbs on Iraq were lifted, the official said by telephone.
Russian companies along with Chinese and French firms are leading the race to tie-up oil deals with Iraq, which holds the world's second largest oil reserves behind Saudi Arabia.
Iraqi officials said last week that a delegation from the CNPC was expected soon in Baghdad to lay down the framework for an agreement to develop the billion-barrel Ahdab field there.
"Iraq has invited us several times to visit and look into oil exploration possibilities, but we have no immediate plan to make such a visit," the official said by telephone.
Iraq has encouraged potential oil production partners to consider developing oil and gas fields once U.N. sanctions are lifted.
Sanctions against investment and trade with Iraq were imposed after Baghdad's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"We won't do anything concrete with Iraq before the U.N. sanctions are lifted," the CNPC official added.
The CNPC official declined to comment on Iraq's remarks that China has moved into contention as the leading candidate to lead development of the prized Halfaya field in southern Iraq.
The oil field was discovered some 20 years ago and could hold commercial reserves of five billion barrels.
"Our technical personnel may have made some contacts with them, which is normal, but they should be only technical-level contacts so far," the official said.
China, a permanent member of the U.N. Security Council, supports easing or lifting the sanctions against Iraq.
